title: Pullback of a global splitting gives its trace sum
statement: Let $f:Y\to X$ be etale [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $F$ an abelian sheaf on $X_{\mathrm{Et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], and $\tau:f_*f^{-1}F\to F$ satisfy $\operatorname{LocalSums}(f,F,\tau)$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image, def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-trace-local-sums]. Let $(V_j\xrightarrow{i_j}Y)_{j\in J}$ be a finite coproduct cofan of open and closed immersions [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion], with inverse $t_j:X\to V_j$ to $i_j$ followed by $f$. Then for every site object $w:W\to X$, $\tau_Wc_{F,W}^{-1}=\sum_j F((\mathrm{id}_W,i_j\circ t_j\circ w)):F(W\times_XY)\to F(W)$, where $c_{F,W}$ is the restriction isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] and the sections are the pullback lifts [def-pc-fibre-product]. The set $J$ may be empty.

source.place: Section 03SH (section-trace-method), paragraph after Definition 03SE; descent details as in SGA 4, Expose IX, 5.1.

proof.text: For the original coproduct cofan, the universal property identifies it with the chosen scheme coproduct. Its underlying space is the disjoint union of the underlying spaces, so its pieces cover and images from different indices cannot intersect.

source.place: Section 03SH (section-trace-method), paragraph after Definition 03SE; descent details as in SGA 4, Expose IX, 5.1.

proof.text: For fixed $W$ let $D_j=V_j\times_Y(W\times_XY)$ and let $a_j:D_j\to W\times_XY$ be the projection. These are open and closed immersions by base change. The pullback range formula identifies their images with inverse images of the original pieces, so they cover and are disjoint. The scheme coproduct criterion for a disjoint covering by open immersions therefore gives their coproduct cofan.

source.place: Section 03SH (section-trace-method), paragraph after Definition 03SE; descent details as in SGA 4, Expose IX, 5.1.

proof.text: Define $\sigma_j=(\mathrm{id}_W,w t_j i_j)$ and $b_j=(w t_j,\sigma_j):W\to D_j$. The pullback projection identities give $b_ja_j=\sigma_j$ and $\sigma_jp_W=\mathrm{id}_W$. The other inverse identity is checked on both projections of $D_j$: use $i_j f t_j=\mathrm{id}_{V_j}$ and the two pullback conditions. Thus $b_j$ is the inverse to $a_jp_W$.

source.place: Section 03SH (section-trace-method), paragraph after Definition 03SE; descent details as in SGA 4, Expose IX, 5.1.

proof.text: Apply the local sum predicate to this cofan and these inverses. Rewrite $b_ja_j=\sigma_j$ to get precisely the asserted finite sum. No inhabitedness is used, so the empty family is included.
